timeline.event: High Court reinstates 30% quota for descendants of freedom fighters
timeline.description: The Bangladesh High Court reinstates the controversial quota system in government jobs, sparking initial discontent among students who view it as discriminatory and limiting merit-based opportunities.

timeline.event: Peaceful student protests begin at Dhaka University
timeline.description: University students initiate peaceful demonstrations demanding quota reform. The protests are organized primarily by students from Dhaka University, Jahangirnagar University, and other institutions across the country.

timeline.event: Protests spread to multiple universities nationwide
timeline.description: The movement gains momentum as students from Rajshahi University, Chittagong University, and other campuses join. Thousands participate in coordinated demonstrations calling for merit-based government recruitment.

timeline.event: Prime Minister makes controversial 'Razakar' comment
timeline.description: PM Sheikh Hasina makes inflammatory remarks comparing quota reform protesters to 'Razakars' (collaborators who sided with Pakistan in 1971), deeply offending protesters and escalating tensions nationwide.

timeline.event: First violent police crackdown at Dhaka University
timeline.description: Police and Bangladesh Chhatra League (student wing of ruling party) attack peaceful protesters with tear gas, rubber bullets, and batons. First casualties reported. Social media shows brutal violence against unarmed students.

timeline.event: Mass arrests and internet shutdown begins
timeline.description: Government orders mass arrests of protest leaders and coordinators. Mobile internet services shut down across major cities. Hundreds detained without proper legal process. Communication blackout intensifies.

timeline.event: Violence spreads to Chittagong and Rajshahi
timeline.description: Armed attacks on protesters intensify in port city Chittagong and Rajshahi. Reports of live ammunition being used. Hospitals overwhelmed with injured students. Death toll rises significantly.

timeline.event: Nationwide internet blackout imposed
timeline.description: Government imposes complete internet shutdown including broadband and mobile data. Social media platforms blocked. International communication severely disrupted. Information blackout prevents real-time reporting of atrocities.

timeline.event: Shoot-on-sight curfew declared
timeline.description: Army deployed with shoot-on-sight orders. Nationwide curfew imposed. People shot in their homes and on rooftops. Eyewitnesses report indiscriminate firing on civilians. Death toll surges dramatically.

timeline.event: Deadliest day - Peak of violence
timeline.description: Bloodiest day of the uprising. Mass shootings in Dhaka's Mirpur, Badda, and other areas. Security forces fire directly at protesters and civilians. Hospitals report shortage of blood and medical supplies. Over 100 deaths in single day.

timeline.event: Supreme Court reduces quotas to 5%
timeline.description: Under mounting pressure, Supreme Court reduces freedom fighter quota from 30% to 5%. However, protesters demand justice for killed students and accountability. Violence continues despite legal victory.

timeline.event: Mass graves and secret burials reported
timeline.description: Reports emerge of authorities conducting secret burials and attempting to hide actual death toll. Families unable to locate missing relatives. Human rights organizations document evidence of mass casualties being concealed.

timeline.event: Partial internet restored, graphic footage emerges
timeline.description: Limited internet access restored. Horrific footage of killings, torture, and brutality floods social media. International community shocked by extent of violence. Calls for investigation grow louder.

timeline.event: International condemnation intensifies
timeline.description: UN Human Rights Office, Amnesty International, and Human Rights Watch condemn excessive force. Multiple countries issue statements demanding accountability. Bangladesh government denies allegations.

timeline.event: Students demand 9-point charter including Hasina's resignation
timeline.description: Movement evolves beyond quota reform. Students present 9-point demand including PM's resignation, justice for victims, and democratic reforms. 'Students Against Discrimination' emerges as key organization.

timeline.event: Mass mobilization despite ban on gatherings
timeline.description: Defying government ban, hundreds of thousands join protests in Dhaka and nationwide. Movement gains support from diverse sections of society including workers, professionals, and civil society.

timeline.event: Protesters blinded by pellet guns and rubber bullets
timeline.description: Increasing reports of protesters losing eyesight from pellet gun injuries. Ophthalmologists report treating hundreds of eye injuries. Many face permanent blindness. Systematic targeting of faces documented.

timeline.event: General strikes and hartals paralyze economy
timeline.description: Nationwide strikes bring economic activities to standstill. Transport, business, and services shut down. International trade through Chittagong port disrupted. Economic pressure mounts on government.

timeline.event: Mass rally of over 1 million in Dhaka
timeline.description: Largest gathering in Bangladesh history. Over one million people flood Dhaka streets demanding Hasina's resignation. Unprecedented unity across age, class, and regional divides. Government's position weakens significantly.

timeline.event: Police and RAB forces begin defecting
timeline.description: Reports emerge of lower-ranking police and RAB personnel refusing to fire on protesters. Some openly express support for movement. Cracks appear in regime's security apparatus.

timeline.event: International media gains access, exposes atrocities
timeline.description: Foreign journalists enter Bangladesh and document aftermath. BBC, Al Jazeera, and others broadcast evidence of systematic violence. Global pressure intensifies. Diplomatic isolation increases.

timeline.event: Army Chief issues veiled ultimatum to government
timeline.description: Army Chief makes public statement suggesting military will not fire on civilians. Interpreted as withdrawal of army support for regime. Political elite understand Hasina's days are numbered.

timeline.event: Cabinet members begin resigning
timeline.description: Several ministers and MPs resign from government positions. Ruling party faces internal dissent. Awami League leaders flee country. Hasina increasingly isolated politically.

timeline.event: Protesters march to Ganabhaban (PM's residence)
timeline.description: Massive march toward Prime Minister's official residence. Security forces do not intervene. Symbolic moment shows regime has lost control. Hasina reportedly in emergency meetings.

timeline.event: Hasina agrees to step down, negotiations begin
timeline.description: Under immense pressure, PM agrees to resign. Backroom negotiations about safe exit. Military facilitates transition. Protesters maintain pressure to ensure she leaves.

timeline.event: Sheikh Hasina flees Bangladesh to India
timeline.description: After 15 years in power, PM Sheikh Hasina flees to India via military helicopter. Students and citizens celebrate in streets. Interim government formed. New chapter begins for Bangladesh.

timeline.event: Interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus sworn in
timeline.description: Dr. Muhammad Yunus takes oath as Chief Adviser of interim government. Students celebrate victory. Focus shifts to justice, accountability, and democratic reforms.

timeline.event: Mass celebrations across Bangladesh
timeline.description: Nationwide celebrations as citizens mark end of autocratic rule. Murals painted honoring martyrs. Discussions begin about prosecuting those responsible for killings. Healing process starts.

timeline.event: First memorial services for martyrs held
timeline.description: Communities across Bangladesh hold memorial services. Families of victims demand justice. Documentation of crimes begins. International tribunals proposed for accountability.

timeline.event: Official death toll announced: 622+ killed
timeline.description: Interim government releases preliminary death toll of over 622, with thousands injured. Actual numbers believed to be higher. Commission formed to investigate all deaths and prosecute perpetrators.

context.title: The July 2024 Bangladesh Uprising
context.background: What began as peaceful student protests against discriminatory quota systems in government jobs escalated into a nationwide movement demanding democratic reforms and accountability. The 'July Revolution' or 'Monsoon Uprising' became one of the most significant mass movements in Bangladesh's history since independence.
context.outcome: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina fled the country on August 5, 2024, ending 15 years of increasingly authoritarian rule. An interim government led by Nobel laureate Dr. Muhammad Yunus was established.
context.trigger: The reinstatement of the 30% quota for descendants of 1971 freedom fighters in government jobs, which students viewed as discriminatory and limiting merit-based opportunities.
context.escalation: Government's violent response, including live ammunition, mass arrests, internet blackouts, and inflammatory rhetoric comparing protesters to 'Razakars' (1971 war collaborators), transformed a reform movement into a demand for regime change.
context.significance: The uprising demonstrated the power of youth-led movements, broke the climate of fear established over 15 years, and showed that even well-entrenched authoritarian regimes can fall when people unite.
keyDemands: Abolition of discriminatory quota system in government jobs
Justice for all martyrs and injured victims
Prosecution of those responsible for killings and violence
Resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina
Release of all detained students and protesters
End to extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances
Compensation for victims and their families

casualties.eyeInjuries: 401 documented cases of severe eye trauma

context.internationalResponse: The uprising received widespread international attention. UN Human Rights Office, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, and multiple governments condemned the excessive use of force. However, neighboring India controversially provided refuge to Hasina after her ouster.
context.aftermath: Dr. Muhammad Yunus-led interim government initiated reforms, investigation into killings, and preparations for democratic transition. Commissions formed to document crimes and prosecute perpetrators. Students played key role in maintaining order post-uprising.
context.remembrance: July 2024 will be remembered as the month Bangladesh's youth reclaimed their future. The martyrs are honored as 'July Shaheed' (July Martyrs), and their sacrifice is credited with ending autocracy and opening path to democracy.
